description: Foundational level for interns, new graduates, and developers with under 1 year of professional experience. Evaluates core concepts, learning aptitude, and structured thinking rather than enterprise production experience.

axes.depth: Foundational understanding of core principles, basic CS fundamentals, standard libraries, and common algorithms.
axes.ambiguity: Low ambiguity expected; questions provide clear inputs, outputs, and constraints with immediate clarification available.
axes.expectedScope: Single function, module, or standard pattern scope; academic coursework or small project implementation.
axes.followUpPressure: Gentle, supportive probing to explore reasoning and verify that the candidate understands their chosen approach.
axes.behavioralExpectations: Demonstrates curiosity, humility, receptiveness to feedback, active learning, and structured communication of school or personal projects.

relevance.name: Relevance & Directness
relevance.description: Answers the fundamental question asked without dodging or reciting unrelated memorized definitions.

anchors.1: Misses the question prompt completely or recites unrelated textbook definitions without addressing what was asked.
anchors.3: Directly addresses the primary question with relevant concepts, though may miss minor edge cases or nuance.
anchors.5: Directly and concisely answers the question, explains why the approach was chosen, and immediately identifies basic constraints.

structure.name: Structural Framing
structure.description: Organizes thoughts logically, using STAR for behavioral questions and step-by-step reasoning for technical problems.

anchors.1: Disorganized stream of consciousness with no clear beginning, reasoning chain, or conclusion.
anchors.3: Follows a recognizable logical sequence (problem, attempt, resolution) with understandable progression.
anchors.5: Exemplary structured narrative: states assumptions upfront, steps through logic methodically, and summarizes the conclusion clearly.

depth.name: Technical & Conceptual Depth
depth.description: Demonstrates genuine understanding of underlying mechanics rather than shallow surface-level keywords.

anchors.1: Uses buzzwords without understanding; unable to explain basic mechanics or why a simple algorithm works.
anchors.3: Understands fundamental mechanics, Big-O complexity for basic operations, and how standard components interact.
anchors.5: Solid grasp of foundational internals, discusses trade-offs between two basic approaches, and correctly reasons about edge cases.

clarity.name: Clarity & Articulation
clarity.description: Explains ideas clearly with accessible vocabulary, low rambling, and audible conviction.

anchors.1: Highly fragmented speech, frequent false starts, excessive verbal fillers, or extreme hesitation that obscures meaning.
anchors.3: Communicates ideas clearly with understandable vocabulary and pacing, occasionally pausing to gather thoughts.
anchors.5: Crisp, concise, and engaging delivery; articulates complex thoughts simply and checks for understanding naturally.

levelFit.name: Level Alignment
levelFit.description: Calibrated against intern/new-grad expectations of curiosity, coachability, and solid fundamental knowledge.

anchors.1: Struggles with basic first-year computer science fundamentals or shows resistance to hints and guidance.
anchors.3: Comfortably meets junior/intern expectations: solves standard basic problems and responds constructively to hints.
anchors.5: Shows maturity well beyond typical new-grad level: anticipates edge cases, writes clean mental logic, and shows high proactive curiosity.
